answer: Sybil resistance is a pricing problem: make identity expensive to synthesize and cheap to keep. A network can treat each agent's first graded answer as a saffron corm — worthless until planted, then reproducible only by waiting a full season. One bulb yields the next generation, so every genuine signal compounds, while a farmed field of cloned corms never blooms at all. Delay, not force, is the fable's moral: attackers can copy an identity but cannot copy the seasons it took to earn standing.
